text: Not sure where to start? Projects → Examples opens a copy of a ready-made project with its documents and scenarios. The example itself is never changed.
Every MSEL row carries a purpose tag, such as core narrative, noise, red herring or pressure. The tags make the exercise design visible and are checked for balance.
Facility facts lists the runways, gates, rooms, systems and phone numbers your documents state. Generation uses only these as real identifiers, so correct the list before you generate.
Search index shows what the generator will find in your plans. If a section you care about does not come up, retitle the document or use the plan's own wording in your brief.
Generate → Give me ideas proposes scenario concepts from your own plans, each citing the sections it would exercise. Add a focus such as "insider threat" to steer them.
In the MSEL editor, lock a row with its padlock to keep it when the MSEL stage runs again, and use Renumber IDs to put inject numbers back in time order.
The Warnings tab lists what the checks found, such as a role with no inject in a phase. Go to row opens the MSEL on that row. Warnings never block saving or export.
Not happy with one part of a scenario? Re-run just that stage with extra instructions, such as "make the red herring more plausible". Locked MSEL rows are kept.
A scenario made by an older version can be repaired in place: the app rewrites only the rows and injects the current checks point at, and keeps the previous version in history.
Long jobs keep running when you move to another screen. The Background jobs list at the bottom of the sidebar shows their progress, and an interrupted generation can resume.
Facilitate runs the exercise: a clock with time jumps, the MSEL timeline with Due now markers, and Show on screen for an inject's media on a second display.
The distribution ZIP has a players folder with only what players may see: the briefing, the forms and the handouts. Controller material stays in the facilitator folder.
Everything works from the keyboard: Skip to main content is the first Tab stop, and dialogs return focus to the button that opened them. The layout adapts at 200% zoom.
Packs add domains, templates, prompts, workflows and example projects. You can install one from a catalog, a file or a URL, and you see a full review before anything is installed.
Before a pack installs, the review lists its license, the app version it needs, its domains, any custom ComfyUI nodes it needs, and the hash of the archive.
A project keeps its own copy of every pack template it uses, so it still renders after the pack is updated or uninstalled.
Packs → Export as pack builds a pack from your own templates, prompts, workflows and one project as an example. Keys and local folder paths are removed on export.
A prompt can be changed for one project (Prompt overrides) or for every project on this computer (Prompts). The most specific layer wins, and the shipped prompt stays untouched.
When changing a prompt, start with a project override, change one thing at a time, and try Extra instructions on a stage re-run first. If an instruction always works, move it into the prompt.
Set aliases in Project settings, such as a short name or the local TV station, and inject templates use them instead of generic names.
Add your organization's logo in Project settings → Brand and locale. Memos, press releases, SITREPs and the exercise plan cover then show it.
Providers → Routing decides which model does each task: ideas, drafting, critique, embeddings, images, video and voice. A project can override any row on its own Provider routing page.
Settings → Local tools detects LM Studio, Ollama, ComfyUI and a local voice server, and can install them from the vendor's official installer after checking its signature.
Add a Limits section to Facility facts, such as "Chlorine, largest container: 1 ton", and the checks flag MSEL rows that name a larger amount.
